items.title: Hospitality Worker Collects $7-Million Lump Sum After Winning Daily Grand's Top Prize
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Mississauga hospitality worker James Lui-Yee won the Daily Grand's top prize of $1,000 a day for life, but chose the $7 million lump sum payout instead. The outlet reported the winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada on Burnhamthorpe Road West. Lui-Yee said he did not check the ticket until two weeks after the draw and initially thought the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation app had made an error. He said his heart raced once he manually confirmed his numbers matched the winning combination at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto. Lui-Yee said he plans to seek financial advice before making major decisions, but hopes to buy a home, invest and travel to Greece, Portugal and Spain, Mississauga.com reported. He also looks forward to buying a new phone and an advanced chessboard, according to the outlet.

items.title: Use-of-Force Training and Anti-Black Racism Among Issues as Francique Inquest Opens
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique has begun after being delayed a day from its original Thursday start. The outlet reported Francique, a 28-year-old Black man, was shot by Peel Regional Police during an attempted arrest outside his home on Jan. 7, 2020, and died in hospital days later. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit later cleared the officers, saying the officer who fired reported fearing for his life after Francique drove toward him, the Star said. The SIU noted there were still questions about the officer's conduct, including his decision to position himself near a fleeing vehicle, according to the report. The inquest will examine police procedures on use of force involving vehicles, oversight of planned arrests, medical care for incapacitated suspects and anti-Black racism, the Toronto Star reported.

items.title: Driver in Custody After Truck Hits Boston Pizza and Police Cruiser at Square One
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a truck crashed into the Boston Pizza restaurant at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga early Friday morning. The outlet reported the vehicle also collided with a police cruiser before the driver was taken into custody. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told insauga.com that officers did not identify the driver beyond confirming he is an adult male. Insauga.com said there is no word yet on potential charges. Photos from the scene showed significant damage to the restaurant, including a section of broken windows, according to the outlet.

items.title: Search Widens to Oshawa and Scarborough for Missing Mississauga Teen Leena
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel police are searching for a missing 14-year-old girl named Leena who was last seen in Mississauga on Wednesday afternoon. Police say she was riding in a black sedan near Rathburn Road and Hurontario Street on Nov. 11. The outlet reported she is just over five feet tall, about 140 pounds, with a medium build, dyed burgundy hair and a piercing on the right side of her nose. She was last seen wearing black pants, black and white shoes and a grey Nike fleece zip-up, according to police. Investigators say Leena is known to frequent the Hamilton, Oshawa and Scarborough areas. Anyone with information is asked to call Peel police at 905-453-2121, extension 1233, Mississauga.com said.

items.title: MiWay Ridership Slide Raises Questions About Future of Hazel McCallion LRT
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, transit advocates Christian Parise and Sylvia Menezes Roberts worry that falling bus ridership in Mississauga and Brampton could undermine the future Hazel McCallion Light Rail Transit line, expected to open by 2028. The outlet reported MiWay saw a 10 per cent drop in passenger boardings in 2025 compared with the year before, along with a $9 million decline in revenue. Both municipalities have cut back service in response, with Brampton Transit suspending four bus routes in April 2026 citing low demand, while MiWay adjusted frequency on several routes, Mississauga.com said. Parise said he grew to value transit as a child riding with his grandmother, who did not drive, but saw it differently once he depended on it in high school. The advocates argue the cuts could weaken ridership just as the new LRT line is set to open, according to the report.

items.title: Jodi Robillos to Chair 17-Member Panel Advising Incoming Mayor Alvin Tedjo
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo has assembled a 17-member transition team ahead of his swearing-in on Nov. 16. The outlet reported the group, which includes developers, community representatives and people connected to provincial and federal governments, met for the first time on Nov. 5. Tedjo told Mississauga News the team is strictly advisory and holds no decision-making authority. He said members are unpaid and were chosen to represent a cross-section of the city, including the non-governmental and social services sectors. The team is chaired by Jodi Robillos, a former commissioner of community services for the City of Mississauga, according to the report. Tedjo announced the transition team on Oct. 29 during his election night celebration at Wildflower Kitchen and Event Space, Mississauga.com said.

items.title: City Marks World Day of Remembrance as Vision Zero Push Continues on Mississauga Streets
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the city will join communities worldwide on Sunday, Nov. 15, in observing the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. The city said the day honours people killed or injured in collisions, along with their families, friends and emergency responders. Roughly 16 million people die each year worldwide in traffic collisions, and road injuries remain the leading cause of death for children and young adults between ages five and 29, the city said. More than half of all road deaths involve pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists, according to the city. Mississauga said it continues pursuing its Vision Zero Action Plan, aimed at eliminating fatal and serious injury collisions on local streets. Throughout 2026 the city kept investing in programs meant to improve safety for everyone traveling by foot, bike, transit, car or mobility device.

items.title: Cost of Living Takes Centre Stage as Peel's Mayors Press New Chair Ahead of Budget
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the mayors of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon issued a joint statement urging Peel's newly reappointed regional chair to prioritize affordability in the region's next budget. The outlet reported Mayor Alvin Tedjo joined Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown and Caledon Mayor Christina Early in congratulating Chair Nando Iannicca on his reappointment while pressing him on cost of living concerns. Housing, groceries and other essentials continue to strain household budgets, the mayors said. Iannicca now holds expanded powers under Ontario's Better Regional Governance Act, 2026, insauga.com noted, including the ability to propose the regional budget and introduce amendments during the year. The outlet reported the chair holds veto power over certain council amendments. The mayors said they look forward to seeing what Iannicca and the province table to ease costs.

items.title: Falconer Drive Sewer Rehab Could Slow Streetsville Traffic to One Lane Through Year-End
items.summary: Peel Region crews are rehabilitating the sanitary sewer along Falconer Drive in Mississauga's Streetsville area, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported work began in October and is expected to continue until close to the end of the year, though the timeline could shift due to weather or other unexpected events. Project officials said crews will clean the sewer pipe and install a new resin lining inside it to extend its lifespan. The region said construction is scheduled Monday to Friday to help shorten the overall work period. Insauga.com reported that traffic on the busy street may be temporarily reduced to a single lane while the work is underway.

items.title: Mississauga Trucker Isik Altinisik Wins Truck Hero Award for Highway 401 Rescue
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga truck driver Isik Altinisik has won the Ontario Trucking Association-Bridgestone Truck Hero Award for pulling a woman from a burning vehicle during a massive highway pileup. The outlet reported Altinisik was delivering fresh food to Ottawa on Jan. 27 when he came upon a chain-reaction crash involving about 50 vehicles on Highway 401 near Trenton amid whiteout conditions, including a 17-vehicle pileup. Rather than driving on, he rushed toward the wreckage to help trapped motorists, insauga.com said. Among them was Theresa Rozendaal, whose SUV had caught fire with flames emerging from the hood and the windshield shattered, according to the report. Altinisik broke the rear window with his bare hands, injuring himself, before pulling Rozendaal from the vehicle and getting her to safety, insauga.com reported.
